text: TFMC Season 5: crafting stations, recipes, and mechanics for the custom systems on the server. More sections will be added as the season goes on. Last modified: 2026-09-19 Getting Started First steps on the server: what to read before anything else. Getting Started Create a character, claim your starter kit, find crafting stations, and learn about custom materials. Character & Identity Who you are: classes, appearance, and the choices that stick with you. RPCharacters Create your character and learn how in-character chat, clues and injuries work. Classes & Character Pick a class, spend attribute points, learn class skills, and level three professions. Equipment Slots Four extra accessory slots: Ring, Amulet and two Artifacts: living in your normal inventory. Server Features & Website Link Letters, lorestones, the animal whistle, and linking your account to the website. Sitting, Crawling & Posing Sit on stairs and slabs, crawl, or strike a pose, for roleplay, not for buffs. Armor Statues A clickable book for posing and configuring armor stands without commands. Bird Mail Send a Letter to another character's bird coop and wait for it to arrive. Professions & Crafting Trades, skill trees, and the systems that turn raw goods into gear. AdvancedCrafting Hammer your own weapons and armor, then invent and name your own metal alloys. Interactive Furniture Place, carry and fill 26 interactive cooking and display furniture definitions. Woodworking Furniture Every one of the 92 decorative furniture pieces you can craft, with a 3D preview of each. Gathering Hidden herb spots in the wild: walk close, notice them, right-click to harvest. Recycler Break a crafted item back down into a share of the materials that made it. Gathering & Farming Where raw materials come from: mining, harvesting, and husbandry. Resource Nodes Place a guild-owned node, pick what it produces, and collect its output every cycle. Crop Harvesting Hoe-based area harvesting and auto-replanting for vanilla wheat, potato and carrot. CustomCrops Watered pots, 30 custom crops, sprinklers and fertilisers: plant, water, harvest. Fishing Rod tiers, bait, hooks and a bite-timing minigame: then sell the catch. Food & Drink Cooking, brewing, and what the results actually do for you. Cooking Furniture cooking: pans, pots, ovens and a 1–5 star quality system. Animal Husbandry Claim animals, keep them fed and clean, and breed for better food and materials. Brewing Ferment, distil and barrel-age real alcohol: with drunkenness that shows. DrinkBuilder Design your own donator drink on the website; it brews like any server recipe. Magic & Knowledge Arcane systems, research, and the strange things buried in the world. Magic Mage weapon parts, spell runes and shrines; attunement is blocked by missing charge sources. Research Deduce hidden aspects at a lectern; paper recipes, project requirements and known reward blockers. Codex Browse lore, character entries and achievements, with missing unlock paths clearly identified. Gem Infusion Infuse 40 gemstones and craft 14 jewellery designs with goldsmithing tools. Archaeology Find a ruin, establish a field camp, excavate by sound, then clean, register, and display recovered finds. Arcane Trace Detector Hunt the server's single hidden source of Arcane Radiation with a clicking, glowing detector. A serverwide loot race. Combat & Danger Fighting, dying, and everything on the server that wants you dead. Guns & Gunsmithing Build Musketeer firearms from parts, then compare ammunition, spread, reload and armour penetration. Infestations Swamp provinces overrun by Bog Monsters: fight the ambient spawns or clear the whole thing with a Lure. Thievery Lock your doors and chests, or break into someone else's: lockpicking, pickpocketing, and consensual robbery. Games Place a table with a Deck of Cards and bet real denars at Blackjack, Hold'em, Five-Draw, or Free play. Vehicles & Machines Mounts, transport, and the machinery that moves you and your cargo. Vehicles & Construction Build, crew, fuel and repair all 21 vehicles, with 3D previews and complete blueprints. Society & Economy Playing with other people: trade, performance, and community systems. Armour Shop Spend a Skin Scroll to restyle the armour or weapon you're holding: pure cosmetics, stats untouched. Factions Found a faction, claim provinces, run a government, and fight scheduled wars over land. Denar Economy Denars: the coins you carry in your pouch, bank at a faction vault, and drop in full when you die. Market Block A sell-only shop block: dump raw materials for denars at a price that sags the more you sell. Musical Instruments Nine instruments turn your hotbar into a keyboard. Only Bards can craft them - anyone can play one. Reference Lookup tables: every material, every station, every number. Materials The full custom material catalogue: Mythril, Coke, and everything else players craft or find. Stations Every crafting station, with an interactive 3D preview where a model exists. Command Index Every command a player can type, A–Z, with the page that documents it and which ones need a permission.

Hands-on blacksmithing: pick a recipe at a Forging Station, feed it raw materials, then physically hammer, carve, etch or sew it with smithing tools. Every ingredient you load adds a number of required hits per tool, and you work the station until each tool's counter is full: it refuses extra hits with a tool that is already done, and refuses to finish while any counter is short. The finished item has a quality grade, stats and socket slots. A second station, the Alloy Forge, lets you invent and name your own metal alloys, which anyone can then use as an ingredient. Last modified: 2026-09-12 Material ranks matter Metals and woods unlock as you advance through the matching crafting profession. If a station refuses a material, continue that profession until you reach its required rank.

Invent your own named metal at the Alloy Forge. Place an Alloy Forge (recipe above). Right-click the forge holding ingredients to load them. The forge tracks one Base: only a metal or wood ingredient can fill it. The only catalysts a metal or wood base accepts are crystal ingredients: the gemstones and other crystals listed above. Leather, feather, wool, paper and enchanted dust are not valid alloy catalysts (config.yml:47-51). Forge it. You need at least 2 ingredients total (a base plus at least one catalyst). If the resulting alloy is new, you get a 60-second naming prompt: run /alloy name <NewName> (letters and underscores only; underscores render as spaces). Once named, the alloy is stored server-wide and anyone can use it as a crafting ingredient. Alloy naming prompt 60 seconds Minimum ingredients 21 base + at least 1 catalyst

Command What it does Notes /alloy name <NewName> Names the alloy you just invented at the Alloy Forge, inside a 60-second naming prompt. Names may only contain letters and underscores. Underscores appear as spaces, and the naming prompt is available to every player who reaches it.

sectionTitle: Crafting a weapon or piece of armor
text: The loop at the Forging Station. Place a Forging Station. Recipe below. Right-click it. A Select Category menu opens (Armor / Weapons / Bows), then a Select Recipe menu. Pick one: a station can only hold one recipe at a time. Right-click the station while holding each required ingredient to load it in. A recipe asks for ingredient types and counts (e.g. "metal ×4"), so you choose which specific metal or wood to use. Right-click the station while holding each required smithing tool to apply hits. Every ingredient you loaded adds its own number of required hits per tool; an on-screen title tracks current/needed for each. Finish the craft once every ingredient is loaded and every hit is completed. Warning Breaking the station mid-craft cancels the project and drops everything you had already inserted.

What you load into a recipe slot decides the finished item's stats, and how many hits of each tool it demands. Base metals and woods: the only ingredients that can be an alloy's base. Every finished craft lands on one of five grades, which decides the socket it gets. Threshold Quality Socket granted 0% Rusted None 50% Tempered Basic Gemstone 75% Polished Polished Gemstone 90% Gleaming Radiant Gemstone 100% Masterwork Mythical Gemstone Note Mage armor uses a separate socket track instead of the Gemstone track above: Minor / Lesser / Greater / Ascendant Armor Rune, at the same thresholds. In both tracks the lowest grade, Rusted, grants no socket at all, so only the top four grades give you one.

All 35 recipes the Forging Station offers, in the order its category menu lists them. Every one of these is a template, not a fixed recipe. The listed quantities are ingredient types, so "4 × Metal" means any four metal ingredients: four Iron Ingots, four Mythril Ingots, a mix, or your own alloy. Which ones you pick is what changes the finished item. The name is generated at craft time, so the Material part of each output name below is a placeholder rather than a literal word. None of the 35 has a crafting time, a cost or a level requirement. Raise livestock for milk, eggs, meat and materials. Claim your animals, keep them fed and clean, then breed successive generations for better genetics. You can own or co-own up to 15 animals. Last modified: 2026-09-23

Breed animals using their normal Minecraft breeding foods. Both parents must be grown, fed, clean and not neutered. Babies inherit a genetics roll based on their parents, with variation; care does not change inherited genetics. Newly claimed wild animals start with 0 to 20 genetics and 0 care. Genetics can reach 1,000 through breeding. Most babies take 1 hour to grow up; chickens take 45 minutes. They keep their baby appearance until that time is up. You can claim babies immediately, but they must mature before breeding, producing milk or eggs, or yielding slaughter goods. Neutering is permanent Right-click an animal you own with the Neutering Tool to prevent it from breeding. This cannot be undone through normal animal care.

Happy means the animal is neither Hungry nor Dirty. Situation What happens Hungry Right-click with Universal Feed. One feed is used to clear hunger. Dirty Right-click with a Glove. The glove is reusable. Happy Care rises by 1 per hour, up to 200. Feeding and cleaning allow care to rise again; they do not instantly add care. Time near the pen An animal becomes Hungry or Dirty after roughly 4 to 8 hours of loaded time, averaging 6 hours. Either state stops care gain. Neglect After 24 hours with an uncleared negative state, care falls by 1 per hour. Leaving the area does not stop this loss. Time away A happy animal can gain at most 8 hours of care while its area is unloaded. After more than 8 hours away, a negative state is added when the area loads again. These are real-world timings. What matters is whether the animal's area stays loaded, including by another player, rather than whether its owner is online. Hungry and Dirty appear beside the animal's name.

Get an Ownership Token, Universal Feed and a Glove. Rename the Ownership Token at an anvil to the name you want for your animal. Right-click the animal with the named token. Animals that need normal Minecraft taming must be tamed first. A successful claim uses the token. Sneak and right-click the animal with an empty hand to inspect its owners, care, genetics, products and growth progress. Return regularly. Use Universal Feed when it is Hungry and the Glove when it is Dirty. You can claim cows, pigs, sheep, chickens, goats, horses, donkeys, mules, camels and llamas. Bees follow normal Minecraft rules and do not count towards your animal limit. Claim newborns before leaving Unclaimed livestock can disappear when the area unloads and loads again. Claim newborns while you are still at the pen. Ownership does not protect animals from players, mobs, fire or other damage.

Animal Products and actions Cow Use an empty bucket for milk, with a 20-minute cooldown per animal. Slaughter yields a beef roast and leather drops. Goat Use an empty bucket for milk, with a 20-minute cooldown per animal. Slaughter yields a goat roast and wool drops. Sheep Shear for normal Minecraft wool. Slaughter yields a mutton roast and wool drops. Chicken Mature, happy chickens lay an egg about every 10 minutes while the area stays loaded. They can also shed feathers. Slaughter yields a chicken roast and feather drops. Pig Slaughter yields a pork roast, with a chance of Enchanted Dust at higher quality tiers. Horse, donkey, mule and camel Slaughter yields a roast of that animal and leather drops. Llama Slaughter yields a llama roast and feather drops. Slaughter goods come from the death of an owned, mature animal; no special slaughter tool is needed. Unowned livestock do not provide these goods. Chicken feather shedding has an 8-hour timer and a 15% chance per eligible check, so feathers are not guaranteed every 8 hours. Eggs and shedding are checked about once a minute while the animal is loaded, grown and happy.

Owned mounts can be ridden by their owners and co-owners. Inspect a mount to see its health, speed and jump stats. Genetics and care contribute to mount stats, so keep breeding stock healthy and check individual animals before choosing your mount.

Right-click your animal with a Co-Ownership Token to link it, then right-click another player with that token to share ownership. A successful share consumes the token. Each shared animal counts towards every owner's limit of 15. Owners and co-owners can feed and clean the animal. Use another named Ownership Token to rename an animal you own.

Breeding raises potential; regular care helps you realise it. For amounts, effective genetics is genetics multiplied by care / 200, rounded down. At 100 care an animal uses half its genetics for yield; at 200 care it uses all of them. Roasts start at 1 carveable cut and gain another cut at each 125 effective genetics, up to 8, limited by the roast's own size. Genetics Food quality ceiling 0 to 199 1 star 200 to 399 2 stars 400 to 599 3 stars 600 to 799 4 stars 800 to 1,000 5 stars Food quality rolls between the star tier of effective genetics and the star tier of raw genetics. For example, 800 genetics and 100 care gives 400 effective genetics, so food can roll 3 to 5 stars. At 200 care, that animal produces 5-star food. Higher genetics also unlock better material drop tiers.

In-game item id: GEIGER_COUNTER. Somewhere in the world, at all times, there is a single hidden source of Arcane Radiation. The Arcane Trace Detector senses where it is: hold it and it shows glowing particle rings and starts clicking, faster and faster as you get closer. The moment you claim it, the source vanishes and reappears somewhere else entirely. It is a serverwide loot race: there is only ever one source, and whoever reaches it first gets to collect it. Last modified: 2026-09-12 Step 1: Get a detector Everything here is crafted at the Engineer Station. Every craft also gives Engineer profession XP. The recharging step needs no profession, so you can trade or buy the detector and fuel from other players and keep recharging it yourself. Unpowered Trace Detector Engineer Station Crafting time: 5 seconds Arcane Crystal 2 Iron Block 2 → Unpowered Trace Detector Arcane Fuel Engineer Station Crafting time: 5 seconds Arcane Crystal Copper Block 4 → Arcane Fuel 16 Yields 16 fuel per craft. Arcane Trace Detector Engineer Station Crafting time: 5 seconds Unpowered Trace Detector Arcane Fuel → Arcane Trace Detector The same recipe recharges a dead detector: no need to re-craft the base item. Step 2: Hunt Hold the detector in your main hand. Particle rings appear around you and the device begins clicking (only you can hear it). Walk and watch the rings and clicking speed. That is your compass. Within about 20 blocks of the source, it is collected automatically. Your detector then runs out of charge and the source respawns to a new location. Step 3: Read the signal What you see or hear What it means 1 ring Over 1000 blocks away. 2 rings Within 1000 blocks. 3 rings Within 300 blocks. Very dark purple, almost black Near the far edge of range (~2500 blocks). Bright purple ~200 blocks out. Turning white Under 200 blocks: the whiter, the closer. Slow clicking (~1 every 2s) Outer limit of the signal. Rapid clicking (a stream) Almost at the source. Step 4: Recharge and go again Claiming the source turns your detector into an Unpowered Trace Detector: "Your Trace Detector has run out of fuel..." You do not need to re-craft the detector: combine it with a single Arcane Fuel at theEngineer Station to power it back up. You can collect 1 source per rolling 24 hours. FAQ "My detector shows nothing." Check that it's the Arcane Trace Detector and not the greyed-out Unpowered version. If unpowered, recharge it with one Arcane Fuel at the Engineer Station. "Somebody else collected the source before me." That happens: there is only one, and it's a race. It has already relocated, so keep hunting; the reading you get now is completely fresh. "I walked right over the source and nothing happened." You're probably at your limit of 1 claim per rolling 24 hours. The source is untouched and still there for someone else. "Can I keep my detector after claiming?" Yes. It just runs out of charge. One Arcane Fuel at the Engineer Station recharges it to full power, so carry spare fuel.
Find an unclaimed ruin, confirm it from soil samples, establish a field camp, excavate by sound, and preserve each find for study or display. Last modified: 2026-09-12

A find is a shape inside the dirt, not a loot block. Expose the shape carefully. When every remaining cube has air on at least one face, those cubes begin dripping. Hold right-click with the brush while aiming at a dripping cube. Looking away pauses that cube; looking back continues it. Keep brushing until one recovered item comes free. A pick never drops the item, and a completely destroyed find drops nothing. The item label tells you whether it is intact, worn, crumbling, or somewhere between. Its starting condition was decided in the ground; careful excavation can preserve it, but cannot turn a naturally damaged piece into a pristine one.

After confirmation, hold the establishment kit and aim at a neighboring chunk rather than the ruin itself. Turn until the camp ghost sits cleanly, then confirm. You become the director, and the tracker will no longer pulse for this ruin. The tents sit beside the dig; the prism marks the ruin ground and the layers below it. Establishing camp does not spend the work day. Use the camp board to read the dossier, manage who may work, review the finds list, and choose Show limits. The glowing cut boundary appears only to you and only briefly. If you have reached your camp limit, close an old camp before claiming another.

Inside the dig site, hold left-click with an excavation tool. The block does not crack like ordinary mining. Listen to the cue, then release the button. Cue Meaning Soft clings, then a louder ready chime Empty fill. Release on the ready chime to lift cubes. Release too soon Nothing leaves. The next hold starts clean. Release too late More cubes leave, giving you less control. The HUD names the stratum and may show how many cuts remain today. Light tools make narrow shafts; heavier tools take wider bites, and a late release always removes more than a timely one. Empty fill can reveal traces of material still touching the hole, which tells you when to slow down. A buried find can be destroyed A find cling means you are cutting into a piece. Punching through it damages the find, and a destroyed cell is gone for good. An ordinary pick can wreck a buried find too, even before anyone establishes a camp.

Make the Archeology Table at a Crafting Table. This workshop is where you make all archaeology tools, including the tracker, prospecting kit, establishment kit, excavation tools, brush, field pencil, and cabinet. Hold the tracker and follow its pulses. They get faster as you approach a ruin that nobody has claimed. If the beeps fade, turn back and try another direction. The tracker stays quiet for a ruin where you already planted a camp. When you are close enough, chat tells you to prospect the ground.

Once every find has been recovered or destroyed, the excavation is exhausted. Close the camp from the board to leave the site and free room for another ruin. You receive a field book; right-click it later to reopen the excavation dossier and finds record even after the tents are gone.

Build any room you like. Shift-right-click a recovered find on a frame, lectern, shelf, armor stand, or a case that accepts plaques to open the same reading available from the camp board. Clicking without Shift keeps the ordinary Minecraft action, such as hanging, rotating, or taking an item. Empty supports and unrelated items do nothing extra.

Use the prospecting kit on shovel-dug earth: dirt, grass, sand, gravel, clay, or mud. Stone and furniture do not count. Hold still while taking each sample; walking away cancels it. Spread samples out and follow the traces until chat confirms the site. Confirmation alone does not claim the ruin.

Take the recovered piece to the cabinet and right-click while holding it. Sneak if you only want the block's ordinary Minecraft use. A dirty piece opens the lab, where each stain names the tool that removes it. A cleaned piece without a drawing can be registered, and an already filed piece opens its reading. Empty-handed clicks do not open the cabinet workflow. To make the drawing, click a field sheet onto the pencil in your inventory, or hold the sheet and use the pencil in your other hand. Sign the sketch, then return to the cabinet and register it with the find in hand.
Pose and configure armor stands with clicks instead of commands: arms, base plate, size, visibility, gravity, and precise rotation and positioning, all from one book. Last modified: 2026-09-19
Command Aliases What it does Notes /tfmc statues None Gives you the Armor Statues book. None
One command hands it to you. Type /tfmc statues to receive the Armor Statues book. It's free and available to every player.

Stand near what you want to change. Place an armor stand, then open the book and click an option: the nearest armor stand is what gets edited. Work your way through the book's pages to change its arms, base plate, size, visibility, gravity, and its exact rotation and position. Full showcase For a walkthrough of everything the book can do, watch "Full Showcase" by ZombieCleo. This is the Armor Statues datapack.

The Armour Shop is a cosmetic wardrobe. Open it, spend a Skin Scroll, and restyle the armour or weapon you're holding: the stats never change, only the appearance (and sometimes the item's display name). Last modified: 2026-09-11
Command Aliases What it does Notes /armourshop None Opens the skin shop: pick Armour skins or Item skins, then a category, then a skin to apply. None

This governs minting your own skin token to upload a custom skin through the website: not browsing the built-in shop. Rank Token cooldown 3D armour helmet: Skin kinds unlocked Commoner Cannot mint tokens No None Noble 28 days No Handheld, large handheld, bow, large bow, crossbow, book Gilded 21 days No Previous tier plus armour sets Ascended 14 days Yes Previous tiers plus 3D items, shields, 3D helmets and guns Legacy 7 days Yes Everything from every lower tier

One command opens the whole shop. Run /armourshop and pick Armour skins or Item skins. Pick a category. The menu shows the categories available to you. Browse the skins available in that category. Click a skin to apply it. If it needs a scroll, the shop checks your inventory for it and for the first item that matches the skin's base set (e.g. a steel chestplate for a steel-tier skin). Missing either one cancels with an error and a sound: nothing is consumed. Applying a skin consumes exactly 1 scroll and merges the new look onto your item, keeping its stats. To go back, use the free Reset to Default category. It covers leather, iron, steel, abyssalite, mythril, mage and infantry base sets. Note Player-forged "custom" gear from the crafting system is skinnable too: every base set's skin list also accepts the equivalent custom-crafted item templates.

Last modified: 2026-09-19

Delivery time depends on how far away the recipient's character last was. The bird's flight time is based on the distance from where you sent it to the recipient character's last known location: roughly a quarter of a second per block, floored and capped. Minimum flight time 30 secondseven at zero distance Maximum flight time 10 minutesany distance past ~2,400 blocks Cost Free If the recipient is online and actively playing that exact character when the bird arrives, they get the letter immediately with a message that a bird has landed at their feet. Otherwise your letter waits, for that character to be played, or for that player to log in: with no expiry. You'll be told your letter is waiting rather than delivered. Warning A letter can only be delivered within the same world the recipient character's last location was in. If they're in a different world, the bird can't reach them and your letter bounces back as undeliverable. Note This is a different system from sealed letters (the writable-book item you sign and hand to someone in person). Bird Mail is specifically for sending a letter to a character who isn't there to hand it to directly, and it can also forward a Discord DM notification (without revealing the sender or the letter's contents) if the recipient has linked their account.

Everything here is block and GUI interaction: there is no /mail command. Get a Letter item and write your message in it, same as writing a normal book. Find a bird mailbox and right-click it: standing still, not sneaking. Sneak-right-clicking does nothing. A small "Bird Messenger" window opens with one open slot. Place your letter into it, or shift-click it in. Anything that isn't a Letter is rejected. Closing that window with a valid letter in it opens a "Send letter" screen: a page of player-head icons, one per character (your own characters are filtered out: you can't mail yourself). Click the head of the character you want to send to, then hit Confirm. The letter leaves your inventory immediately and a bird flies off with it. If you close the picker without confirming, you get your letter back. Bird Mailbox Right-click the mailbox to send a written Letter.
Last modified: 2026-09-11

Command Aliases What it does Notes /brew help [page] /brewery help, /breweryx help Shows the paged command list. Available to every player. /brew info /brewery info, /breweryx info Shows your current drunkenness percentage and quality. None

Donator ranks can add a custom drink through the DrinkBuilder guide. Each submission uses one creation token, whose cooldown is shared with custom skin creation. Rank Creation interval Drink customisation Noble Every 28 days 1 name colour; standard bottle and message Gilded Every 21 days 2 name colours; custom bottle texture Ascended Every 14 days Up to 8 name colours; custom bottle texture and message Legacy Every 7 days Up to 8 name colours; custom bottle texture and message

Ferment, then optionally distil, then optionally age. 1. Ferment. Place a cauldron over a fire or campfire, fill it with water, then right-click it in your main hand with ingredients to throw them in. Right-click with a clock/watch to read the current cook time. 2. Bottle. Right-click the cauldron with a glass bottle to draw off one brew. 3. Distil (optional). Put the bottle in a Brewing Stand with glowstone dust; it runs the recipe's configured number of distill runs. 4. Age (optional). Build a barrel: vanilla barrels work too, up to 6 brews at once, and right-click it to open. Signs on custom barrels must contain the barrel keyword. 5. Seal (optional). A Sealing Table (a re-skinned Smoker) strips a brew down for selling in shops. 6. Drink. The label always shows quality; the exact alcohol number is hidden but an indicator is shown, and drinking prints a status message.
1 barrel year 20 real minutes Hangover length up to 7 days Large barrel size 3 inventory rows Small barrel size 1 inventory row

RPCharacters is who you are on this server. Your roleplay chat, injuries and deaths belong to a character you create, not to your Minecraft account directly. In Survival, you cannot do much of anything until you have one. Last modified: 2026-09-15 Warning With no active character, almost every command is blocked: you can still run /rpcharacter ..., /roll, and the chat-channel commands, and nothing else. Making a character is not optional.

Plain typing talks in-character. Everything else is a command. Whatever you type without a command goes to your default channel, which starts as regular in-character speech (rp). Change your default with /channel <id> (bare /channel shows your current one), and hide or show a channel in your own view with /channeltoggle <id>. Channel Command Range What it's for In-character speech /rp 15 blocks Normal talking as your character Shout /shout 24 blocks Raised voice Yell /yell (/y) 48 blocks Shouting at the top of your lungs: bold red Whisper /whisper (/wh) 2 blocks Quiet, only for someone right next to you Local OOC /looc 20 blocks Out-of-character chatter with people nearby Global OOC /ooc Unlimited Server-wide out-of-character chat: works with no character Action /me 20 blocks Emotes and actions, shown as narration Scene /scene 20 blocks Scene-setting narration, no speech bubble Warning Speech is also affected by walls and distance: muffled or distant speakers can appear partly garbled, or show up simply as ::: if you are too far to make them out clearly.

Investigation is passive by default, active if you want it faster. Characters can leave 2-10 personal clues around the world, plus every character automatically leaves a subtle racial tell. Clues are found passively over time just by being nearby, or actively by holding a magnifying glass (four tiers exist, better ones see further and find things faster) and right-clicking to search. Clue potency fades over time, so an old clue is harder to read than a fresh one. /rpcharacter clues opens your own clue list.

One command starts a long guided creator: expect to spend real time on this. Type /rpcharacter create to begin. You will be walked stage by stage through: an out-of-character age gate (18+), your character's name (typed in chat), class information and selection, race selection, character age, a set of trait choices (homeland, cataclysm, reclamation, motivation, gift, virtue, combat, physical, celestial), attribute allocation, personality, an optional evil archetype, a permanent injury roll, an optional prosthetic, a written description, an opening clue, and finally your wardrobe. Use /rpcharacter next, back, help and cancel to move through it. Once you have a character, /rpcharacter menu opens a menu of your characters so you can switch between them (on a cooldown: see below), and /rpcharacter kit starter claims your starting supplies: an iron hunting knife, 32 gold coins, 256 bread, a writable book, a bundle and a brown bed. The starter kit can only be claimed once per character, with a 48-hour cooldown. Death and injury are part of the roleplay, not just a stat penalty. Injuries can be healing (temporary) or permanent, and range from a broken arm to full blindness: each comes with real stat penalties while it lasts. Two players can arrange a consensual roleplay injury with /rpcharacter injure <player>: you pick the injury from a GUI, then the target has to confirm it within 30 seconds. If your character dies, a grave chest appears with a hologram showing who killed you: right-click it to recover your things (or let someone else rob it). Graves never expire on their own. A Grave Insurance item, if you have one, recovers your newest grave from anywhere. Healing injury duration 72 hours Consensual injury range 10 blockswith a 30s confirm timeout Grave hologram radius 32 blocks

A quiet way to check who you're talking to. Sneak, hold nothing in your hand, and right-click a player to print their character card : name and whatever they have chosen to show. It only works with an empty hand while sneaking, so it will not fire by accident.

Small touches you can set once your character exists. /rpcharacter namecolour, gender, description, birthday let you fill in and adjust who your character is after creation. Descriptions must contain 32 to 256 characters. The name-colour tool supports the number of colour stops listed for your rank above. Players with Noble, Gilded, Ascended, or Legacy rank can use colour codes.

Choose one of seven combat classes, gain class levels, improve attributes, and level three gathering professions. Last modified: 2026-09-18

The active story act sets the highest class level you can reach. Act Class level cap Prologue 6 Act 1 11 Act 2 16 Act 3 21 When the server advances to a new act, the class level cap rises. Some item drops are also limited by act, so later materials may become available as the story progresses.

Seven selectable classes cover different equipment and play styles. Class Equipment Class skills Play style Archer Shortbows, Longbows, Crossbows, Light Armor 8 Deadly marksmen, wielding bows with precision. They deal sustained damage from a distance, and are excellent at maintaining a favourable position, making them ever-reliable. Bard Lutes, Light Armor 8 Charismatic minstrels, wielding Mana through music. They can provide magical blessings and hamper enemy mobility. Lore warns: "Mages are expensive to gear!" Musketeer Pistols, Rifles, Shotguns, Rocket Launchers, Infantry Armor 0 Excel at the usage of advanced guns and gadgets. Though lacking skills, they manufacture custom firearms, many of which deal armor-piercing damage. Warrior One-Handed Weapons, Two-Handed Weapons, Shortswords, Battle Standards, Medium Armor 8 Mobile masters of combat, weaving attacks with an array of flexible skills to inflict great damage.

New characters are taken to class selection during creation. Read each class description and choose the equipment style you want to use. Open /player to review your level, professions, attributes and party information. Open /attributes to spend attribute points and /skills to manage class skills. In the skills menu, shift-left-click a skill, then left-click a skill slot to bind it. Right-click a slot to unbind it. Press F, the swap-hands key, then press the number shown on the action bar to cast a bound skill. Note Musketeer and Mage do not have class-skills.

Cooking has no menu and no crafting table. It is a set of real furniture props you place in the world: a pan, a pot, a cutting board, an oven, a milling stone, a fire pit with a spit, a butter churn, a sausage maker. Put ingredients on them, work the station, and the food item you get back tracks its own freshness, cooked state, seasoning and a 1–5 star quality rating: all shown in the item's name and lore. There is nothing to type; everything is a right-click. Last modified: 2026-09-20

Each right-click with the Cutting Knife on a roast or sausage chain takes one cut off, in this order. Sequence Cuts Yields in order Whole Chicken 6 Chicken Leg ×2, Chicken ×3, then 2 Bone Beef / Venison Roast 8 Beef ×7, then 4 Bone Sausage Chain 5 Sausage ×5
Fire Pit Whole Chicken, Beef Roast, Venison Roast Frying Pan Chicken, Chicken Leg, Steak, Beef, Venison, Pork, Sausage, Cut vegetables Pot Cut vegetables

Recipe Input cut_vegetables Any raw vegetable (Carrot, Potato, Tomato, Onion, Lettuce, Cucumber, Corn, Beetroot, Pumpkin) chop_vegetables Any cut vegetable chop_olive Olive chop_pistachio Pistachio chop_rhubarb Rhubarb chop_garlic Garlic Olive, Pistachio, Rhubarb and Garlic skip the cutting step and go straight to chopped : every other vegetable above is cut first, then optionally chopped again.

The furniture and the two clicks that drive every station. 1. Place the furniture you need: Frying Pan, Pot, Cutting Board, Fire Pit, Milling Stone, Mixing Bowl, Oven Bottom + Oven Top with a Bread Tray, Butter Churn, Sausage Maker, Meat Hook, or a plain vanilla Cauldron. 2. Right-click the furniture while holding an ingredient to place it into one of the furniture's slots. 3. Right-click with an empty hand to take the item back out, or to operate the station (churn, turn the spit, stir). 4. Stations that need heat must sit above a heat source. For soup, place a Pot directly on an Oven Bottom, add logs and light them. 5. Cooking ticks once per second, so every time listed below is in real seconds, not ticks.

A simple carrot and potato soup to get you started. Ingredients: 2 Carrots, 2 Potatoes, a Water Bucket and wood logs for fuel. Equipment: Cutting Board, Cutting Knife, Oven Bottom, Pot, Flint and Steel, Masher, Ladle and a Bowl. Put 2 carrots on the Cutting Board and cut them once with a Cutting Knife. Take the cut carrots off the board. Put 2 potatoes on the cutting board and cut them once with the Cutting Knife. Take the cut potatoes off the board. Craft an Oven Bottom and place it, then put a Pot on top. Right-click the pot with a Water Bucket to fill it. Right-click the Oven Bottom while holding wood logs to add fuel. Right-click the logs inside the oven with Flint and Steel to light them. Wait for the water to boil, then add either the cut carrots or the cut potatoes. Right-click the vegetables in the pot with a Masher to mash them into soup. Add the other cut vegetables and mash them in the same way. Once the soup has finished cooking, right-click it with a Ladle to take a serving. Pour the soup into a Bowl, then right-click to eat it.

What to hold and what happens at each station. Station Held item / action Result Cutting Board Hold the Cutting Knife and interact Runs a cutting/chopping recipe on up to 4 slots at once: all 4 must be the same ingredient. Frying Pan Place food, needs heat below; take out by hand Cooks over time; burns if left on too long. Pot Add a Water Bucket, then cut vegetables Makes boiled foods and soups. A node is a guild-owned production site. Place one in a chunk, choose what kind of operation it is, fit it out, feed it materials, and it produces resources on a repeating cycle. Last modified: 2026-09-18

Upgrades are paid from the guild bank and are the same for every node type. Level 1 Starting level Level 2 40 Level 3 80 Level 4 160 Level 5 320 Level 6 640 Level 7 1,280 Level 8 2,560 Level 9 5,120 Level 10 10,060 Each figure is the cost of upgrading to that level from the one before it.

Transfer Node marks the node as claimable. The next guild leader who interacts with it claims it for their guild. Delete Node cannot be undone. Only the node block is refunded; its level and fittings are lost. Only members of the owning guild can change a node.

Crafted at a plain Crafting Table. Anyone can make one. General Node Crafting Table Requires: None Oak Planks Oak Planks Oak Planks Oak Planks Gold Ingot Oak Planks Oak Planks Oak Planks Oak Planks → One General Node can run any of the six node types.

You must belong to a guild; a one-person guild is enough. Note Each guild can own only one node. Place the General Node on the floor. Each chunk can hold only one node. Right-click the node to open its menu, then pick a node type. Choose a production focus and the node's fittings, such as tools, a refinery, lighting or irrigation. Put a Barrel directly under the node and stock it. Fittings that have a running cost take their materials from that barrel every cycle. Put a Hopper directly above the node to catch what it produces. Without one, the output drops on top of the node. Activate the node. The menu shows its efficiency and what the last cycle extracted. Note Deactivate the node before you change its type, focus or fittings, upgrade or downgrade it, or delete it. Deactivating resets the current cycle and refunds that cycle's cost.

A General Node can run any one of these. The focus decides what the node produces. Denars are the server's money. You carry them as a pouch balance or as physical gold and silver coin items, and you can also stash them safely in your faction's bank. Every trade at a Market Block, every coin you find mining or farming, and every faction wage or tax runs through this system. Last modified: 2026-09-12

Every player has two separate balances. Pouch Carried moneyDropped in full on death unless you keep your inventory Bank Stored moneySafe on death: requires a faction bank chunk to use Warning Your pouch is not safe on death. Unless you have the faction "keep pouch" perk or keep-inventory is on, dying zeroes your entire pouch and drops it as coins where you died. Your bank balance is never touched by death.

Coins are real, tradeable items: picking one up credits your pouch automatically. 1 Gold Denar = 100 Silver Denars. The first few steps every faction goes through. /faction create <name> founds your faction and makes you its leader. Stand in a province and run /faction setcapital <name>. This is required before you can claim anything else. Stand in a province adjacent to land you already own and run /faction claim (leader only). Invite others with /faction invite <player>; they accept with /faction join <name>. Note Untitled land is capped at 5 provinces. Claim a 6th and you're told to form a County first: see the tier table below.

A guild is a sub-organisation inside your faction, useful for trade income. Any non-leader member can /guild create <name> to start a sub-guild with its own bank, leadership, and trade branches (Bureaucracy, Guild Halls, Workshops, Storehouses). The faction leader runs the "base guild" automatically. From /faction menu you can also open government, laws, taxes, council and elections: under a democracy the leader can't be set directly; players vote at voting booths instead. Resource nodes Guilds also own resource nodes: production sites that turn out ores, crops, wood or stone on a repeating cycle. You must be in a guild to place one, and a one-person guild is enough. Craft a General Node and place it. A guild can own only one node, and each chunk holds only one. Run it as an Ore Mine, Magical Mine, Farm, Plantation, Forestry or Quarry, then pick what it focuses on. Upgrades from level 1 to 10 are paid from the guild bank, so the guild needs a bank with funds in it. Only members of the owning guild can change a node. A guild leader can claim a node that another guild has marked for transfer.

Built by a faction leader with /faction construct, in an owned, non-water province. Type Radius Upkeep / day Build time Vehicle slots Fort 80 blocks 50 d 5 days 8 static emplacement + 2 land vehicle Port 80 blocks 20 d 3 days 8 ship Airport 80 blocks 35 d 3 days 10 aircraft Note Berthing a vehicle requires the vehicle's owner to be online and consent. An unpaid vehicle (see /faction vehicle maintenance pay) cannot be repaired.

A guild can found a mercenary company and hire it out to other factions. Inside a guild, /company found <name> buys a charter; the company leader invites recruits and drafts a contract with /company draft, then sends it to a buyer faction with /company offer <faction>. Buyers browse the market with /mercenaries and hire with /mercenaries hire <company>.

Battles are scheduled events, not spontaneous fights. When a war has been declared, check /war list. Form a squad with /warband create <name>, then join a scheduled fight with /battle join <battleId> when its window opens, or a campaign raid with /raid join during its 60-second muster. Retreating a warband mid-battle is locked for the first 20 minutes.

CustomCrops replaces vanilla farming with 30 custom crops planted in watered pots. Nothing here is a vanilla crop block: every crop is a small model sitting in a pot, and it only grows while that pot is watered. This is where almost every fruit, vegetable and spice used by Cooking and DrinkBuilder comes from. Last modified: 2026-09-20

'Regrows' means harvesting rolls the plant back to an early stage instead of destroying it, so it keeps producing. Apple Banana Cactus Fruit Cherry Grape Lemon Lime Orange Peach Pineapple Pistachio Plum Strawberry Tomato Corn Cucumber Garlic Lettuce Mustard Seeds Olive Onion Rhubarb Rice Yeast Basil Black Pepper Cinnamon Nutmeg Spice Leaf Vanilla Apple Profession Fruits Regrows Yes The Fruits profession unlocks 14 crops, Vegetables 10, and Spices 6: without the matching permission you can neither plant nor harvest that crop.

Till, water, plant, wait, harvest. 1. Till ground into farmland as normal: pots sit on top of vanilla farmland. 2. Water the pot: right-click it with a water bottle/potion, or fill a Watering Can at water and right-click pots to soak a 3×3 area. Pots also absorb rain and adjacent water on their own. 3. Right-click the watered pot holding the crop's seed item. You need that crop's profession permission, or you're told you can't plant it. 4. Wait. The crop advances a growth stage only while the pot's water is above a threshold. 5. Optionally speed things up with Bone Meal or a fertiliser. 6. Right-click the fully grown crop with an empty hand (or break it) to harvest: you get 2–4 produce plus a seed back.

Water is the one thing every crop needs: no water, no growth. Item Detail Watering Can Holds 20 water, uses 5 per click, waters a 3×3 area. Refill by right-clicking a water source (+5 per click). Watering Can

CustomFishing replaces vanilla fishing with a skill minigame: when something bites, you play a timing minigame, and what you get depends on your rod tier, the biome you're fishing in, and any hook and bait you have equipped. Win the minigame and you get the loot; lose it and the fish gets away. Last modified: 2026-09-12

1. Get a rod: there are four tiers (below). 2. Optionally right-click the rod while holding a hook to attach it; right-click the rod again to remove it. Its remaining uses show in the rod's lore. 3. Optionally put bait in your off-hand. 4. Cast normally. The wait for a bite is 5–30 seconds base, and never less than 2.5 s or more than 60 s after every modifier is applied. 5. When it bites, one of 17 minigames fires, at a difficulty set by your rod tier.

Each rod pairs with one hook. The hook adds durability and shaves time off the wait. Games turns any block into a card table. Place a deck, pick a game from a GUI, and bet real denars against other players (or the house) at Blackjack, Tenceur Hold'em, Five-Draw, or a no-rules Free play table. Cards float in front of you as 3-D displays that only nearby players can see, and money actually changes hands: winnings are taxed like any other income. Last modified: 2026-09-12

The only game with a table actually standing on the server today. While betting is open, right-click your own box on the felt holding coins. Click again to add more. When your name comes up, right-click the shoe for a card, or type hit, stand, double, or split in chat. Those words only register on your turn. /games bet hit does the same thing. The dealer reveals and draws to 17. This house does not hit soft 17. A win returns double your bet; a natural 21 on the first two cards pays 3:2; a push returns your bet. No insurance and no surrender are offered. To deal by hand, stand at the dealer's spot and right-click the shoe; right-click again to hand it over. A dealer runs /games bet min <n>, /games bet max <n>, /games bet open, /games bet close, then right-clicks the shoe. Some tables deal themselves : betting opens automatically once the first real bet lands.

Everything else at a table: placing it, dealing, betting coins, drawing, discarding, revealing, taking the free-play pot: is clicks and chat words, not commands. The chat words a table recognises, only on your turn, are hit, stand, double, split, check, call, raise, fold, and draw (Five-Draw stand-pat only). Command What it does /games Prints the usage line appropriate to your permissions. /games help Opens the "Table games" index book. /games help <blackjack|poker|draw|freeplay> Opens that game's rule book. /games bet min <n> Sets the table minimum, as the dealer standing at the shoe. /games bet max <n> Sets the table maximum. /games bet open Opens betting for a round. /games bet close Closes betting. /games bet hit | stand | double | split Blackjack action on your turn. /games bet check | call | fold | raise Tenceur Hold'em / Five-Draw action on your turn. /wager <amount> Proposes the item you are currently holding as a stake; the table votes on it. /wager accept Votes yes on a proposed wager. /wager decline Votes no on a proposed wager.

No rules, no turns, no dealer. Right-click the shoe empty-handed for a card. Click cards then right-click the shoe to discard them. No limit on how many you hold. Right-click the felt with coins to add to the middle. Warning Sneak + right-clicking the shoe picks up the entire pot. Play with people you trust.

Tenceur Hold'em and Five-Draw share the same seating and betting flow. Right-click the felt with coins to sit down. Once two players are seated, anyone at the table can right-click the shoe to deal. Bet by pushing coins onto the felt first, then saying the word in chat: check, call, raise, fold. The table reads how many coins you actually put out, so saying "raise" with nothing on the felt does nothing. The dealer button shown above the table moves one seat after every hand; it sets who acts first. Five-Draw only: on your draw turn, click the cards you want to discard, then right-click the shoe for that many replacements. To stand pat, type draw in chat: chat only, there is no /games bet draw. Calling with less than you need puts you in for what you could manage: side pots are created and you can only win what you matched. Walking off forfeits this round's stake; earlier rounds' stakes do not return. Warning The blinds shown above a Hold'em or Five-Draw table are advisory only. Nothing is taken from you automatically: whoever owes a blind has to put the coins out themselves.

Rules shared by every table, whichever game you pick. Cards render fanned in front of you, visible only within 48 blocks. Left-click a card in your fan to inspect it. Press your swap-hands key (F) to flip your whole hand face-up for the table. Right-click the shoe (the deck sitting on the table) to draw, deal, or act. Right-click the felt while holding coins to bet. Walk more than 6 blocks from the table and your cards return. This round's stake comes back with them. Only whole denars go on a table; silver bits are refused. The house's own help book puts it plainly: "Only whole coins go on a table. Silver bits are no good." Winnings are subject to the usual citizen tax, same as any other income.

Place a table and invite other players to join. Hold a Deck of Cards. Right-click a block. A game-select GUI opens with four icons. Pick a game. Blackjack opens a table-options GUI (min bet, max bet, house settings) first; Poker, Five-Draw and Free play arm placement immediately. Click the spot to place the table. Sneaking cancels an armed placement. Picking the table back up drops the Deck of Cards item again at the table's origin.

Betting something other than coins. Hold the item, type /wager <amount>, and the table votes on whether it counts (a 30-second window). If accepted, you have 10 seconds to click the felt with that same item. With only one other player at the table, a wager auto-accepts if nobody else has bought in. Note Place a Deck of Cards to set up a table and choose a game. Note The deck is themed to server lore: the four suits are cerrith, mitlan, oseni and seithr, rather than hearts, clubs, diamonds and spades.

Gathering spots spawn hidden in the wild. Your character notices one when you walk close enough: a message tells you something is nearby, and a faint particle ring marks the spot. Right-click it to harvest whatever loot it rolls. Last modified: 2026-09-15

Passive discovery is rolled once every 12 seconds for everyone within range. Detection range 6 blocks Wisdom bonus +2%per point of Wisdom Intelligence bonus +1.5%per point of Intelligence Herborist bonus +1%per level of the Herborist profession

Discovery is tracked per roleplay character, not per account. Spots spawn on their own on eligible blocks, invisible until discovered. Every 12 seconds, every player within 6 blocks of a spot has a chance to notice it. On a success: "You notice something glinting nearby..." A discovered spot shows a small particle ring so you can find it again. Right-click the spot to gather. Loot is rolled and the items pop out with a little velocity. If the roll comes up empty: "Nothing to gather here." The spot is consumed: gathering it once uses it up, and its chunk goes on cooldown.

What you actually get for harvesting a spot. A forest-herbs spot gives 1–2 loot rolls, and every roll currently comes from the same pool: 2–4 Stack of Gold Denars (worth 10 denars each, so 20–40 denars per roll).
Turn blank gemstones into stat-bearing Infused Gemstones at an Enchanting Table. Goldsmiths can then build jewellery around one infused gem at a Smithing Table. Last modified: 2026-09-12

Goldsmith profession required Any player can infuse gems. Crafting jewellery requires the Goldsmith profession. Right-click an empty Smithing Table and choose one of the 14 projects. Right-click with each required gold material to deposit one item per click. Follow the exact recipe; all gold belongs to one material bucket, but the finish check still requires the correct mix. Right-click with one Infused Gemstone. Every project requires exactly one. Any of the 40 infused gems is accepted. Left-click with the Goldsmith Hammer, Small Goldsmith Hammer and Tinker Tool to fill their respective counters. Requirements are calculated from deposited materials. Right-click with the Branding Tool to inspect material, gem and hit progress. When every requirement is exactly complete, left-click with it to finish and collect the jewellery dropped on the bench. To cancel, shift-left-click with the Branding Tool. Materials and the gem return to inventory; overflow drops at your feet. Warning Finishing requires exact ingredients and exact hit counts. There is no 40% partial finish. Breaking a bench refunds deposits to the person who breaks it. Bring a Blank Gemstone from the 40-entry catalogue and an Infusion Ticket to any Enchanting Table. An ordinary vanilla jewel will not work. Hold a blank gem and right-click the table to deposit one. Repeat up to 10 gems. Deposited gems leave your hand. Hold the infusion token and left-click the table five times. After the first hit, the batch is locked and cannot accept more gems. The fifth hit consumes one token for the entire batch. Collect every infused gem that drops above the table. Drops start after 30 ticks, then appear every 2 ticks. A Legendary result is announced server-wide. Batch size 1-10 gems Finish 5 left-clicks Token cost 1 per completed batch

Basic, Polished, Radiant and Mythical are socket types, with ten gems in each. Common, Rare, Epic and Legendary are independently rolled rarities. The resulting name is, for example, Legendary Infused Ruby. Match the Gemstone Type to the receiving socket. Names, lore and rarity are restored when the gem is unsocketed. Right-click to harvest; some hoes can also plant. 1. Right-click (break) a mature vanilla crop with a hoe. Every mature crop within the hoe's radius harvests at once, drops go straight into your inventory, and each spot is auto-replanted after a short delay. 2. With a hoe that can plant, you can also plant seeds across every empty patch of farmland inside the radius in one action. This never damages the tool. 3. Immature crops are never touched by an area-harvest. 4. Unbreaking still saves durability normally. The only crops this affects: Wheat, Potatoes, Carrots, Beetroots, and Nether Wart.

Whole map provinces can get overrun by monsters: on this server, every infestation you will meet is swamp-flavoured and shown on the map as "Bog Monsters". Walk into one and it spawns ambient enemies around you on its own; place a Lure and you can fight a single big wave that, if you win, clears the province outright. Last modified: 2026-09-12

What actually happens once you step into an infested province. Walk into an infested province at night. Ambient monsters spawn in a ring around you, up to a cap, on a fixed interval: both scale with severity. To go further, place a Lure. This opens a 20-second join window: leave the province, or right-click the Lure to commit to the fight. If you neither join nor leave, the lure starts without you and you take 2 deserter damage per check for staying nearby uncommitted. Clear every mob and the infestation is cleared outright; dying, running out the timer, or leaving means the infestation remains. Logging out mid-Lure does not save you: there is only a 300-second grace period, after which you are marked to die on your next login. Note Placing a Lure in a clean (non-infested) province does nothing. Only one Lure can be active in a province at a time.

Infestations are province-wide and only active at night. Infested provinces are shown on the server's web map with a severity label. Ambient spawning and Lure waves only happen while it is night in-world: during the day an infested province is quiet.

Two reasons to seek an infestation out rather than avoid it. An infested province is simply more dangerous ground. It keeps spawning monsters around you for as long as you stand in it, at night. That is a steady stream of kills if you want one. Committing to a Lure raises the stakes further: a single scripted wave sized to the province's severity, fought to a clean win-or-lose result, with the province's infestation lifted entirely if you clear it.

Magic is the mage path. You build a staff, wand or blade out of parts at a Magic Station, slot spell runes into it, and then attune it to one of ten elements by feeding it magical energy you gathered from a shrine. Your character also carries a personal Resonance score in every element, and a weapon will simply refuse to fire if your Resonance is too low for what it holds. Last modified: 2026-09-18

Three weapon shapes, each wanting a different set of parts. Archetype In-game name Melee: Parts it needs Staff Mage Staff No Core, Handle, Tome x3 Wand Wand No Core, Handle, Tome Sword Mage Blade Yes Core, Handle, Tome

Hold the weapon and use the rune's casting key. The default is right-click. To change a rune's casting key, hold the rune and use /magic rune keybind. What you see Why What it costs you *Whiff* Your Rift rolled against you (or the rarer "Too many staffs" message). Mana and the cooldown, both already spent. *Refused* Your Resonance is below what the weapon asks, or the weapon holds no element at all. Nothing. *Damaged* A config change left the weapon holding runes it can no longer seat. Nothing, but the weapon will not cast until you reclaim its runes. A refusal explains itself in chat: "The weapon asks for {element} {need}. You carry {have}.", but only once every 30 seconds per weapon and element, so do not expect a message on every click. To fix a Damaged weapon, right-click an empty Magic Station: it works the loose runes free and hands them back.

A charge is a consumable, not an artifact. Put it on a pedestal in a shrine and it is imprinted with every element that shrine scores, then filled from it. Charges are crafted at the Rune Station from Enchanted Dust: 4, 8, 12 and 16 dust for tiers I to IV. Enchanted Charge I Rune Station Crafting time: 10 seconds Enchanted Dust 4 → Enchanted Charge I Enchanted Charge II Rune Station Crafting time: 10 seconds Enchanted Dust 8 → Enchanted Charge II Enchanted Charge III Rune Station Crafting time: 10 seconds Enchanted Dust 12 → Enchanted Charge III Enchanted Charge IV Rune Station Crafting time: 10 seconds Enchanted Dust 16 → Enchanted Charge IV A weak shrine cannot fill a high-tier charge. That is the tier gate. The band printed on a charge ("Cerrith II") is just a readout of how much aura it holds: under 10 shows a dash, 10 is I, 40 is II, 75 is III, 110 is IV.

View your Resonance profile and change a rune's casting key. Command Aliases What it does /magic rune keybind None While holding a rune, use this command to change its casting key. /resonance /res Opens your Resonance profile: a bar per element, your Equilibrium (Corruption vs Tranquility), your Mental Points, and the Surge / Flow cast-mode toggle.

The intended loop, start to finish. Be a Mage. The Mage class is what gates Mage Staffs, Mage Wands, Mage Blades and Mage Armor. Its own description warns that mages are expensive to gear. Open /resonance and pick a cast mode: Surge ("Power now. Corruption later.") or Flow ("Slow start. Stronger at depth."). Flow is the default. Craft and place a Magic Station, then interact with it to open the assembly menu and build a weapon out of parts. Slot runes into the weapon's sockets. This is where spells come from; a weapon with no runes casts nothing. Build a shrine and put an artifact on a pedestal in it to soak up aura. Imprint and fill a charge on that same pedestal. Spend the charge on the weapon at the station, which starts the orb minigame that decides how much of the charge actually sticks. Hold the weapon and use the rune's casting key to cast. The default is right-click.

Shrines do not only fill artifacts. Standing in one and meditating is how you raise your own Resonance. Resonance per orb hit 4.0 Mental Point cost per hit 1 Mental Point pool 150shared with Research Regeneration +10 / houroffline too Mental Points (also called Focus) are a shared pool spent by both Magic meditation and Research experiments. Wisdom adds +0.5 per hour per point and Intelligence +0.25. A full pool of 150 takes fifteen real hours to refill and buys 150 orb hits. That is 600 potential Resonance before element caps, shared-artifact division and session limits. Resonance bleeds, and artifacts get tired of you Resonance decays at -0.02 per real hour, so a mage who stops meditating slowly slides back. Worse, an artifact you meditate on gets muffled: it gives less and less over 24 hours of use, and takes a full 7 days to recover. If several people are attuned to one artifact, the yield is divided between them. Storing an artifact in a chest raises its muffle, silently. Safe places are your own inventory, a pedestal, an artifact display, or an item frame.

Applying a charge to a weapon does not just write the attunement. It starts a timed minigame, and the charge is spent up front whether you win or not. Orbs circle you. Pale blue orbs are good: hit enough of them before the window closes and the weapon settles, holding a percentage of the charge. Rust-orange orbs tear the weapon: each one you hit adds +5 persistent Rift, capped at 100. Missing a good orb costs 8% of the run. Disconnecting mid-run ends it with whatever you had. A charge can exceed your Resonance Right-click the prepared weapon on its station with the charge to start. If the charge demands more Resonance than you have, the configured warning lists each shortfall and asks you to right-click again to commit anyway. That second click spends the charge. Rift per bad orb +5capped at 100 Rift removed per later recharge 10never on the first charge Rift persists until reduced by a later recharge Rift is the percentage chance a cast simply fails. A failed cast still spends the mana and still starts the cooldown. You can only ever grind it back down 10 points at a time, and only on a later successful charge.

A socket takes a rune of its own tier or any tier below it. It never takes a bigger one. Craft quality of the gear Socket it gets Rune that fits Rusted None Nothing Tempered Minor Minor Polished Lesser Minor, Lesser Gleaming Greater Minor, Lesser, Greater Masterwork Ascendant Any tier The socket comes from how well the piece was crafted, not from its material. Iron Mage armor can take an Ascendant Armor Rune, but only if that piece came out Masterwork. A Tempered iron piece has a Minor socket, so a Minor Armor Rune is the most it will ever hold. Armor runes go on Mage armor only. Every other armor piece has a Gemstone socket instead, and an armor rune will not fit it. Armor runes and weapon runes are separate: an armor rune never fits a staff, wand or blade, and a spell rune never fits armor. A smaller rune in a bigger socket works, but it uses that socket up. If a piece has several sockets, the rune goes into the smallest one that can hold it. Check the socket line in the item's lore before you spend the dust. It names the biggest size the piece accepts. Quality is decided while smithing, see Advanced Crafting.

Five words you need before anything else makes sense. Term What it means Element One of ten flavours of magic: Cerrith, Oseni, Seithr, Mitlan, Bloodmagic, Spirit, Arcanum, Illusion, Necromancy, Shadowmancy. Resonance A 0-100 score your character holds in each element separately. It decides whether a weapon will accept a charge, and it scales the mana cost, damage and cooldown of your spells. Aura The physical resource. It lives inside artifacts and charges, is gathered from shrines, and is spent to attune a weapon. Aura in an artifact never decays. Socket A hole in a finished weapon that one spell rune fits into. Sockets come in four sizes: Minor, Lesser, Greater and Ascendant, and a socket takes a rune of its own size or smaller. Attunement Locking an element into a weapon by spending a charge on it. Until you do, the weapon holds no element and refuses to cast. It is per character, not per account Resonance and Equilibrium are stored against your active RP character. A second character starts from zero. /resonance refuses to open at all without an active character.

A Market Block is a shop you place yourself: right-click it and sell raw materials for denars. It only buys: there is no way to purchase items back from it. The more of one material the block has already absorbed, the less it pays for the next bundle, and that price slowly recovers if you leave it alone. Last modified: 2026-09-20

Craft it, place it, and start selling. Craft a Market Block (recipe below) and place it. Right-click it to open Market Categories: Farming, Mining, Woodcutting, Fishing, Other. Click a category to see its trades, each showing the item, its current price, and a demand bar. Click a trade to sell a full bundle of that item for denars, paid straight into your pouch. Market Block Crafting Table Requires: None Ink Sac Paper Oak Planks Oak Planks Oak Planks Oak Planks Oak Planks → Synthetic Ink can replace the Ink Sac. Use one Oak Plank in each of the five plank slots.

Instruments turn your hotbar into a keyboard. Hold one in your off-hand and press 1 through 8. Hold Shift for a second layer of chords or higher notes. There are nine instruments, each with a completely different sound. Other players hear you from about 64 blocks away. All nine are crafted at the Instrument Station and crafting them requires the Bard class, but anyone can play one, so an instrument you are given or buy works fine. Command Aliases What it does Notes /instruments keybinds None Prints the full note and chord layout for the instrument currently in your off-hand. You must be holding an instrument in your off-hand, or it just tells you so. Permission instruments.use, default true - no normal player is ever blocked. /instruments list None Prints the name of every instrument that exists on the server. Needs nothing in hand. Permission instruments.use, default true - no normal player is ever blocked.

"My instrument makes no sound." Three things, in order. One: your Jukebox/Note Blocks volume slider must not be at zero: notes play in the Records category, not Master or Ambient. Two: the instrument must be in your off-hand. Three: press 1–8; slot 9 is the reset slot and plays nothing. "Can I craft an instrument without being a Bard?" No: all nine recipes require the Bard class. "Can I play an instrument without being a Bard?" Yes. The instrument items carry no class requirement and no stat requirement of any kind, and nothing checks your class when you press a key. Instruments are tradeable, so a non-Bard handed one plays it exactly as well as its maker. "Do I need a permission?" No. Both instrument commands are available to every player.

Put the instrument in your off-hand. Your main hand is irrelevant. Press number keys 1 to 8 to play notes. The scale runs: 1=C, 2=D, 3=E, 4=F, 5=G, 6=A, 7=B, 8=C (an octave up). Hold Shift and press 1 to 8 for the second layer. On most instruments that's a full chord; on the Flute, Trumpet and Bagpipe it's the same scale an octave higher, giving sixteen notes total. After every note your selection snaps back to slot 9. This is deliberate, and lets you hit the same note twice in a row instead of the key doing nothing the second time. Whatever sits in slot 9 is therefore what bystanders see in your main hand while you play. A single note particle appears above your head with each note, so everyone can tell it is you.

The Recycling Station breaks a crafted item back down into a share of the materials it took to make it. A pristine item gives back the most; a worn-down one gives back less, and a fully broken item gives back nothing at all. Last modified: 2026-09-12
Built on a vanilla crafting table. Recycling Station Crafting Table Requires: None Iron Ingot Iron Ingot Iron Ingot Iron Ingot Oak Planks Oak Planks Oak Planks → Recycling Station

Right-click the placed station to open it. Right-click the Recycling Station. A 3×9 GUI opens. Drop the item you want to break down into the input slot. An item that cannot be recycled at all is rejected with "That item cannot be recycled here." The middle columns of the GUI preview exactly what you would get back. If recycling it would return nothing, the preview says so and the confirm button is blocked. Click confirm. Your outputs are spawned and kicked out of the station, and you get "Recycling complete." If you close the GUI with an item still sitting in the input slot, it is returned to you.

Three sources are checked, in this order. Source How the return is worked out Weapons and Armor Refunds the exact ingredients (or alloy components) that were used to craft it. Guns Refunds materials according to the weapon recipe and its remaining durability. Items with a dedicated recycling recipe Returns materials from its recycling recipe.
Research is an item-based deduction puzzle. Make a research paper at a Cartography Table, study it at a Lectern, and test materials to uncover and fill its hidden aspects. Last modified: 2026-09-12

Rule Meaning Primary / secondary aspect An item contributes more strongly to each primary aspect than to each secondary aspect. One item can contribute to several aspects. Rejected An aspect outside the hidden recipe is rejected after enough testing. An experiment containing only rejected aspects is blocked. Undiscovered Aspect Its row appears after you make some progress toward the required points. Intelligence makes it appear sooner. Confirmed Its identity appears after further progress. Intelligence makes it appear sooner. Confirmation is not completion: keep filling it. Product reveal The product appears after enough aspects are confirmed. Intelligence can make it appear sooner, but early reveal is not assured. Completion Every hidden aspect must reach its full required points. Total points are not an experiment count, because tests may contribute to multiple aspects. A concrete experiment example Arcane Crystal is a primary Arcane item, so it supplies 2 Arcane points when tested. Crying Obsidian is secondary Arcane and supplies 1. These are distinct items, so each can be tested once. The Arcane Crystal project requires 3 Arcane points, plus its Earth, Energy and Machine requirements.

Maximum Focus 150Stored per RP character; shared with Magic meditation Each experiment 1 point Base refill 10 per real hourRegenerates offline; 15 hours from empty to full Wisdom adds 0.5 points per hour per attribute point; Intelligence adds 0.25. The regeneration interval is one hour. When exhausted, the lectern tells you that you are too tired to research. The aspect table counts distinct primary and secondary items; it is not a recipe or a list of required quantities.

sectionTitle: Make a paper and start a project
text: Sneak-right-click a Cartography Table to open the Research Station. Combine one vanilla Paper and one Alchemy Powder for one Parchment Paper. It takes 5 seconds. Combine one Parchment Paper with the subject ingredient. Ordinary papers take 5 seconds; an Unknown Research Paper takes 15 seconds. Every station recipe grants 10 Herborist EXP. Recipes hide when you lack their ingredients. Hold the resulting paper and right-click a Lectern. Each lectern has one owner, so find another lectern if one is occupied. A Staff Runestone can start its own project without first becoming a paper. Choose an experiment item, inspect its point preview, then confirm. Each different item may be tested once per project. Items with no aspect tags cannot be used. Use the Testing, Confirmed and Rejected labels to guide your next experiment. Fill every required aspect completely, then collect the result that drops above the lectern. It is not placed directly in your inventory. Warning Breaking the lectern destroys the project. The Scrap button also destroys it after a confirmation and does not refund the project.
Last modified: 2026-09-18

There is a cap on how many animals one player can keep. Each player can own at most 15 animals. Every animal counts towards it, horses and other mounts included, so you cannot keep a large flock of one kind, such as 50 chickens for eggs. Plan your livestock around the 15 slots.

Command What it does Notes /linkdiscord Requests a one-time Discord link code and prints it click-to-copy in chat. Run /linkdiscord <code> in the Discord server to finish linking, usually within about a second. /unlinkdiscord Removes your Discord link. Re-applies the Survival Discord-verification gate. /token Shows the token actions available to you. None

Ordinary-looking blocks open custom crafting menus. Right-click (or shift-right-click, depending on the block) a station block, for example, a brewing stand for the alchemy station, and a custom crafting-station GUI opens instead of the vanilla menu. See the Crafting Stations guide for the full list of stations and what each one crafts.

Add a permanent line of lore or a new name to an item. Craft a Lorestone or Namestone at the Tool Station using the recipes below. Pick up a Lorestone or Namestone on your cursor, then click it onto a single item in your own inventory (it must not be stacked). A chat prompt appears: type the text within 60 seconds, or type cancel. A Lorestone adds a line of lore; a Namestone renames the item instead. If anything goes wrong the stone is refunded rather than wasted. Lorestone Tool Station Crafting time: 5 seconds Gold Ingot → Lorestone Namestone Tool Station Crafting time: 5 seconds Iron Ingot → Namestone Prompt timeout 60 seconds Max line length 100 characterscolour codes count Max lore lines per item 10

Not to be confused with BirdMessenger's mail: see below. Letter Crafting Table Requires: None Paper Paper Paper Paper → Letter Write in the Letter and sign it to seal it. Craft four Paper in a square to make a Letter. Write your message in it and click "Sign." It becomes a sealed letter instead of a normal written book. Anyone who right-clicks it reads it, and the letter is then marked opened. Right-clicking it onto a lectern or a chiselled bookshelf does not break the seal, so you can use those as regular storage without accidentally reading someone's letter. Note This is a different system from BirdMessenger, which delivers letters to a specific character over real time via a bird coop. TFMCCore's sealed letters are just an item: sending it anywhere is still up to you.

Your in-game account and the TFMC website are separate until you link Discord. Type /linkdiscord and the server prints a click-to-copy code with instructions. Run /linkdiscord <code> in the Discord server, and within about a second the game confirms the link and opens access to Survival. /unlinkdiscord removes the link again and reapplies the gate. /token create profile mints a code to sign into your website profile. Selecting Remember me keeps that session on this device for 30 days. /token create skin and /token create drink mint codes for uploading a custom skin or a custom drink, but these two share one cooldown, and how often you can mint one depends on your rank. Rank Skin/drink mint cooldown Commoner Cannot mint Legacy 7 days Ascended 14 days Gilded 21 days Noble 28 days Note Bird-mail arrivals are forwarded to your Discord messages when your account is linked. The message does not reveal the sender or the letter's contents.

Right-click it to find your mount. Right click an Animal Station to craft an Animal Whistle. Sit on furniture, lie down, crawl, or strike a pose: small physical touches that make a scene feel real. It's free for every player; nothing here needs a rank. Last modified: 2026-09-11

Command Aliases What it does Notes /sit None Sit down where you're standing. None /sit toggle None Turns your click-to-sit (right-clicking stairs/slabs/carpets) on or off. On by default. /lay /glay Lie down on your back. None /layback /glayback A lie-back pose. Not listed on the in-game /help menu. /bellyflop /gbellyflop A bellyflop pose. None /spin /gspin A spinning pose. None /crawl /gcrawl Drop to a prone, crawling position. Double-tapping sneak to crawl is turned off here, so this command is the only way in. /crawl toggle /gcrawl toggle Would toggle double-sneak-to-crawl. Double-sneak-to-crawl is disabled server-wide anyway.

Go prone without needing a low ceiling. Type /crawl to drop to a prone, crawling stance; sneak to stand back up. Double-tapping sneak to start crawling is turned off on this server, so the command is the only way in. Click-to-sit reach 3 blocks Damage while seated Doesn't stand you up

For scenes that need more than sitting. /lay puts you on your back facing up. /layback, /bellyflop and /spin are other poses. While posed you cannot interact with blocks, items or other players, so it's meant for a still moment, not mid-fight. Sneak to get back up.

The easiest way in: just right-click. Right-click a stair, slab, carpet or snow layer with an empty main hand and you sit down, snapped neatly to the block. You must be within 3 blocks to sit by clicking. Only the bottom half of stairs and slabs works: a top slab or an upside-down stair won't seat you. You can also just type /sit. To get up, press Sneak/Shift. Taking damage will not knock you out of a seat, but breaking the block underneath you will. If click-to-sit ever annoys you (e.g. you keep accidentally sitting on stairs while building), turn it off with /sit toggle: typing /sit still works to sit on command.
